title: Fonctions L / Équation fonctionnelle des fonctions L (cas géométrique) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (geometric L-functions): D is a decomposition group at a point, I ⊂ D the inertia subgroup (normal in D), and D/I is generated topologically by Frobenius. E is a finite-dimensional representation of D in characteristic 0, for example an ℓ-adic local system at a point. The local factor of the L-function involves the inertia invariants E^I, with φ ∈ D/I acting on them. Grothendieck wants a formula for Tr(φ | E^I) in terms of traces on E itself.

Steps on the page:
(1) Additivity. If E = ⊕ E_i, then Tr_{E^I}(φ) = Σ_i Tr_{E_i^I}(φ).
(2) Choice of U. Choose U ⊂ I, a subgroup acting trivially on E, open (hence of finite index in I) and normal in D. This is possible when I acts on E through a finite quotient. Then I/U is finite of order N = card(I/U), and D/U acts on E.
(3) Projector. E^I is the image of the averaging projector π = (1/N) Σ_{i∈I/U} e_i.
(4) Trace. Take any g ∈ D/U lifting φ. Because I is normal in D, π commutes with g, so Tr_{E^I}(φ) = Tr_E(π g) = (1/N) Σ_{i∈I/U} Tr_E(i g).
(5) Boxed formula. The elements i·g run exactly over the lifts of φ to D/U, so
 Tr_{E^I}(φ) = (1/N) Σ_{ψ ∈ D/U, ψ ↦ φ ∈ D/I} Tr_E(ψ).
(6) Final remark (partly illegible). Tr_E(ψ) for ψ ∈ D/U equals Tr_E(ψ') for any ψ' ∈ D projecting to ψ. Hence the right-hand side is the average of Tr_E over the lifts of Frobenius, and it does not depend on the choice of U. This prepares the expression of local Euler factors at ramified points as averages of traces over Frobenius lifts, of the kind used in Lefschetz–Grothendieck trace formulas for L-functions with ramification.
errors: The formula needs an open subgroup U ⊂ I acting trivially on E, i.e. inertia acting through a finite quotient. For a general ℓ-adic representation, Grothendieck's monodromy theorem gives only quasi-unipotent inertia action. In that case one must first pass to the semisimplification or treat the unipotent part separately; the page does not discuss this (it may be an implicit hypothesis on the illegible lines).
N must be invertible in the coefficient field. This is fine in characteristic 0 (Q_ℓ, C), but the projector argument fails for modular coefficients when the characteristic divides N.
There are minor notational slips: the summation index is written alternately as ψ and ψ_α, and as D/U and DU.

ideas.what: Trace of Frobenius on inertia invariants written as the average of traces over all lifts of Frobenius modulo an open subgroup of inertia acting trivially, via the averaging projector
ideas.modern_name: Averaging formula for local Euler factors / trace on E^I as a mean over the Frobenius coset (Artin-type local factor computation)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Artin's definition of L-factors at ramified primes); standard in Serre's Corps locaux / Représentations linéaires and in Deligne's work on local constants
ideas.where_published: Comparable computations of local terms appear around SGA 5 and SGA 4½ (Deligne, 'Rapport'); not certain this exact formula is printed in a Grothendieck text

ideas.what: Additivity of the trace on invariants over a direct-sum decomposition
ideas.modern_name: Additivity of traces / exactness of invariants for finite groups in characteristic 0

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine, correct computation of the trace on inertia invariants as an average over Frobenius lifts, standard since Artin. It is useful context for Grothendieck's work on the functional equation of geometric L-functions but contains nothing new. One minor archival point: the sheet appears to be written on the back of a Bourbaki typescript (Commutative Algebra ch. VII, draft n° 392), whose typed text bleeds through and is what the 'neighbouring page' transcriptions show.
transcription_corrections: The superscript written 'E^U' in the trace formulas is most likely E^I (inertia invariants): the left side is Tr_{E^I}(φ) with φ ∈ D/I, and U is the auxiliary open subgroup.
Line 5 reads approximately 'Or soit U ⊂ I [ouvert] agissant trivialement sur E, [distingué dans D]', not 'si ... qui irréductible'.
Line 6 reads approximately 'alors on considère D/U' / '[opère] sur D/U'.
In 'Im π' the projector is over I/U ('π = (1/N) Σ_{i∈I/U} e_i, N = card I/U'), and 'L_projection' refers to the projector, not a separate L.
The text 'représentation invariante' in line 1 is doubtful; the word is illegible and may be '[l']induite' or similar.
The 'previous' and 'next' page transcriptions are the bleed-through/verso Bourbaki typescript (Algèbre commutative ch. VII, n° 392), not Grothendieck's L-function notes.
